content.value_statement: Long AI conversations can become slow, costly, and less reliable as context grows. This skill provides practical techniques for compression, masking, caching, and partitioning.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to compact long conversation history and tool outputs.
Provides observation masking patterns for verbose tool results.
Describes cache-friendly prompt ordering for stable prefixes.
Outlines context budget allocation and trigger thresholds.
Includes Python utility examples for token estimates, masking, and cache metrics.
Shows when to partition work across focused sub-agents.
limitations: Token counting uses approximate heuristics unless integrated with model-specific tokenizers.
The sample summarization logic is demonstration quality, not production-grade semantic compression.
Cache metrics require integration with actual inference infrastructure to be accurate.
The skill provides guidance and utilities, not a complete agent framework.

use_cases.title: Reduce Long Conversation Cost
use_cases.description: Apply compaction and masking when accumulated history or tool output drives token usage above target budgets.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Latency
use_cases.description: Design stable prompt prefixes and context ordering to improve cache reuse across repeated agent tasks.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Split large tasks into isolated sub-agent contexts and aggregate concise results for the coordinator.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Context Pressure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment of a long AI workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this AI workflow and identify where context grows fastest. Recommend one simple optimization to reduce token use without losing important state.

prompt_templates.title: Design Compaction Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Create practical rules for summarizing history and tool output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create compaction rules for this agent. Include what to preserve, what to summarize, when to trigger compaction, and how to verify quality after compaction.

prompt_templates.title: Build Cache-Friendly Prompts
prompt_templates.scenario: Reorder context for better prefix stability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this prompt structure for cache stability. Move stable elements earlier, isolate dynamic values, and explain how the changes improve cache hit rates.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Context Partitioning
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design for long-running agent systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a context partitioning strategy for this multi-step task. Define sub-agent boundaries, retained state, result aggregation, and failure recovery checks.

output_examples.input: A support agent keeps all ticket logs, search results, and conversation history in one context.
output_examples.output: Recommended output: a context budget, a compaction trigger at high utilization, masking for older search results, and a short retained state summary.

output_examples.input: A batch agent repeats the same tool instructions but adds a timestamp near the start of each prompt.
output_examples.output: Recommended output: move the timestamp outside the stable prefix, keep tool instructions first, and track cache hit rate before and after the change.

output_examples.input: A research workflow fails when documents, notes, and synthesis steps share one long context.
output_examples.output: Recommended output: split retrieval, document review, and synthesis into separate contexts, then aggregate cited summaries into the coordinator context.

best_practices: Measure token use and quality before adding optimization machinery.
Preserve task goals, user preferences, recent turns, and critical decisions during compaction.
Keep stable prompt components before dynamic content to improve cache reuse.
anti_patterns: Do not compact system instructions or active task constraints.
Do not mask observations that are still needed for current reasoning.
Do not add partitioning overhead when context limits are not constraining performance.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps reduce token use, latency, and quality loss in long AI conversations or agent workflows.

faq.question: Does it increase the model context window?
faq.answer: No. It helps use the available context more effectively through compression, masking, caching, and partitioning.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Python utility examples for token estimates, observation masking, budgets, and cache metrics.

faq.question: Is the sample code production ready?
faq.answer: No. The utilities are reference implementations and should be adapted with real tokenizers and infrastructure metrics.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid adding these techniques when context size is not causing cost, latency, or quality problems.
